title: Chronicles of the Clockwork Archive
author: Clara Thorne
synopsis: In the brass-domed metropolis of New Aethelgard, junior archivist Beatrice Quill discovers a forbidden brass cylinder containing the recorded final breath of the city's vanished founder—and a blueprint proving the Great Sky-Engine is counting down to zero.

glossary.desc: The colossal geothermal pendulum suspending New Aethelgard above the Cloud Sea.

reviews.text: A completed steampunk mystery that actually sticks the landing! Beatrice is an unforgettable protagonist.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Vault Seventeen
chapters.content:
Every clock in the Grand Archive ticked three milliseconds out of sync with the city outside, a deliberate quirk engineered to prevent resonant vibration from shattering the glass memory-cylinders on the upper galleries.

Beatrice Quill knew the rhythm of those ten thousand pendulums better than she knew her own pulse. Which was why, at half past eleven on a fog-drenched Tuesday, she immediately noticed the faint metallic *whir* coming from Vault Seventeen—a vault officially empty since the Great Fire of '74.

Lifting her brass oil-lantern, she turned the skeleton key. The heavy iron latch yielded with a puff of dry cedar dust. Inside, resting alone on a velvet plinth, sat a walnut phonograph no bigger than a jewelry box, its copper horn polished bright as a fresh sovereign.

Engraved around the winding crank were nine words in her late grandfather's crisp draftsman's hand:

*Do not play this until the barometer drops below twelve.*

Beatrice glanced down at the pocket barometer clipped to her waistcoat. The brass needle was trembling violently against eleven-point-four.

comments.text: What a hook! The atmosphere in Chapter 1: Vault Seventeen completely pulled me in. Thanks for the chapter!

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Voice Beneath the Gears
chapters.content:
She wound the crank three careful turns and lowered the diamond stylus onto the grooved brass cylinder.

First came a hiss like escaping steam, followed by the unmistakable low rumble of the Great Sky-Engine turning miles beneath their feet. Then a voice—calm, cultured, and terribly urgent—filled the dusty stone chamber.

*"If the needle has passed twelve, my dear Beatrice, then the Council has lied to the citizenry for forty years. The Sky-Engine is not an eternal dynamo. It is a counterweight, and someone on the Upper Spire has begun cutting the anchor cables."*

The lantern flame guttered violently as boots clattered down the iron spiral staircase two floors above.
